Base directory for this skill: /Users/eric/.claude/skills/merging-branches-safely

# Merging Branches Safely

## Overview

Investigate merges **before** touching the working tree. Use `git merge-tree` to predict conflicts without mutating state, classify each conflict, surface a resolution proposal, and only run `git merge` / `git rebase` after the user approves — or immediately if preflight predicts no conflicts.

**Core primitive:** `git merge-tree A B` simulates a full merge and prints conflict markers. No index, worktree, or HEAD changes. It is the single most important tool in this skill.

**Announce at start:** "Using merging-branches-safely — starting with read-only preflight."

## The Four Phases

```dot
digraph merge_flow {
    preflight [shape=box, label="Phase 1: Preflight (read-only)"];
    predicted [shape=diamond, label="merge-tree predicts conflicts?"];
    classify [shape=box, label="Phase 2: Classify + propose"];
    approved [shape=diamond, label="User approves resolution?"];
    execute [shape=box, label="Phase 3: Execute merge/rebase\n+ verify"];
    commit [shape=box, label="Phase 4: Commit (no push)"];
    revise [shape=box, label="Revise proposal"];

    preflight -> predicted;
    predicted -> classify [label="yes"];
    predicted -> execute [label="no"];
    classify -> approved;
    approved -> revise [label="no"];
    revise -> classify;
    approved -> execute [label="yes"];
    execute -> commit;
}
```

### Phase 1 — Preflight (ALWAYS, read-only)

Never start a merge/rebase before this phase completes. Collect, without mutating state:

```bash
# Fork point
BASE=$(git merge-base <ours> <theirs>)

# What each side added
git log --oneline <theirs> ^<ours>          # incoming commits
git log --oneline <ours> ^<theirs>          # our commits

# File-level scope
git diff --stat $BASE..<ours>
git diff --stat $BASE..<theirs>

# Overlap set — files touched on both sides
comm -12 \
  <(git diff --name-only $BASE..<ours> | sort) \
  <(git diff --name-only $BASE..<theirs> | sort)

# Conflict prediction (merge)
git merge-tree <ours> <theirs> 2>&1 | grep -E "^CONFLICT|^Auto-merging"

# Conflict prediction (rebase) — simulate each commit replaying
for sha in $(git log --reverse --format=%H $BASE..<theirs>); do
  git merge-tree <ours> $sha | grep "^CONFLICT" && echo "  ^ at $sha"
done
```

Report to the user: incoming commits, scope, overlap, predicted conflicts (or "none").

If no conflicts predicted → skip to Phase 3.

### Phase 2 — Classify + propose (only when conflicts predicted)

For every overlapping file (conflicting **and** auto-merging), inspect both sides' diffs:

```bash
git diff $BASE..<ours>   -- <path>
git diff $BASE..<theirs> -- <path>
```

Tag each file with one of:

| Tag | Meaning | Default resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `orthogonal` | Both sides edit the same region with semantically independent changes (e.g., one adds an import, one adds a different import nearby) | Combine both |
| `supersede` | One side's change replaces the other's intent (e.g., feature deleted a function main renamed) | Take the winning side and justify |
| `semantic-overlap` | Both sides modify the same behavior — no mechanical answer | Escalate: present options, let user pick |
| `silent-semantic` | Git reports a **clean auto-merge** but the combined code is broken (renamed identifier still referenced, type contract mismatched, invariant violated) | Flag and propose fix — these are the dangerous ones |
| `generated-artifact` | A conflict in a file produced from source, not hand-authored — `pnpm-lock.yaml`, other lockfiles, generated schemas/types | Don't resolve the artifact. Resolve its **source** (the `package.json` files), then **regenerate** it — see Phase 3 |

Auto-merged files still need a classification. `silent-semantic` only surfaces if you look. Skipping this check is the most common failure mode.

**Stop and ask.** Present:
- Per-file tag + proposed resolution (one line each)
- Any `silent-semantic` flags prominently
- A single "approve / change / abort" question

Wait for approval. Do not start the merge.

### Phase 3 — Execute (only after approval, or immediately if Phase 1 was clean)

```bash
git merge <theirs> --no-commit --no-ff   # or: git rebase <theirs>
```

For each conflicting file, apply the approved resolution with the Edit tool (not by hand-rewriting full files).

**`pnpm-lock.yaml` (and any `generated-artifact`) is the exception — never Edit it.** It is generated from the `package.json` files. Resolve every conflicting `package.json` first, **merging both sides' intent** — main's dependency changes *and* the branch's — not one side wholesale. Then discard the conflicted lockfile and regenerate it:

```bash
# Pick the lockfile side that has been re-resolved more recently:
#   merge (main into branch): git checkout --theirs  → uses main's lockfile
#   rebase (branch onto main): git checkout --ours   → also main's lockfile (rebase inverts the semantics)
# Either way, you want main's transitive baseline — Renovate keeps it fresh.
git checkout --theirs pnpm-lock.yaml
pnpm install --lockfile-only --recursive --ignore-scripts --ignore-pnpmfile
pnpm dedupe --ignore-scripts         # only if the repo dedupes its lockfile (check renovate.json5 postUpdateOptions)
git add pnpm-lock.yaml
```

**Side choice matters.** `pnpm install --lockfile-only` is conservative — it keeps every transitive resolution that still satisfies the merged manifests' ranges. If the *branch* side is stale, its older (sometimes vulnerable) transitives still satisfy the caret ranges, so they survive regen + dedupe. Starting from main's lockfile gives pnpm the freshest baseline to reconcile against. `pnpm dedupe` consolidates duplicates but **does not** upgrade resolutions — it cannot fix this on its own. OSV scans on the PR will surface the resulting vulnerability delta against main if you pick the wrong side.

For the full command matrix — lockfile-only-update PRs, `lockFileMaintenance` PRs, the verify-the-bump-landed grep — see `rebasing-renovate-prs-locally`, the specialization for when the whole PR *is* a dependency bump.

Then:

```bash
# Re-verify no markers remain
grep -rn "^<<<<<<< \|^======= $\|^>>>>>>> " <touched-paths>

# Also open each auto-merged overlap file and confirm semantics
# (silent-semantic hides here — auto-merge being clean is not a safety check)

# Run project verification
<project-typecheck-command>
<project-test-command-if-user-has-that-convention>

# If the merge touched package.json / pnpm-lock.yaml: typecheck + test are NOT enough.
# A re-resolved dependency tree can break the bundler only. Also run:
<project-build-command>
pnpm deps:lint                       # syncpack — catches override/specifier drift
```

If verification fails, fix before committing. Never `--no-verify` to ship a broken merge.

### Phase 4 — Commit (never push)

```bash
git add <resolved-paths>
git commit --no-edit          # merge message pre-filled; rebase: git rebase --continue
```

Stop here. Pushing is a separate user-authorized action.

## Guardrails

- **Never `git merge --abort` as an exploration tool.** That's what `git merge-tree` is for. Aborting after a partial merge loses signal and adds noise to the reflog.
- **Never start a merge/rebase before Phase 1.**
- **Never use `-X ours`, `-X theirs`, or `--no-verify` to skip resolution.** They hide conflicts; they don't resolve them.
- **Dirty working tree at Phase 1 → stop and surface.** Do not stash silently; the user may have in-progress work.
- **Auto-merge clean ≠ semantically clean.** Every overlap file gets a tag, including auto-merged ones.
- **Never Edit `pnpm-lock.yaml` (or any generated artifact) to resolve a conflict.** It's derived from the manifests — fix those, then regenerate. A hand-merged lockfile drifts from what the resolver produces and breaks `--frozen-lockfile` installs.
- **One tag per file, written down.** Forces naming before fixing.
- **The approval gate is bypassable in two cases:** (1) Phase 1 predicts zero conflicts, or (2) the user has given explicit pre-authorization in this turn (e.g., "merge and commit, no need to confirm"). Absent either, pause. A generic "merge X into Y" does not count as pre-authorization — users often expect to see the preflight before resolution begins.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Why it fails | Do instead |
|---|---|---|
| Running `git merge` to "see what conflicts" | Mutates state; forces `--abort`; pollutes reflog | Use `git merge-tree` — zero side effects |
| Skipping auto-merged files in Phase 2 | `silent-semantic` conflicts hide here | Every overlap file gets a tag |
| Resolving before user approval | Treats "merge branch X" as resolution authorization | Approval gate is mandatory when conflicts are predicted |
| Inferring conflict type from the conflict markers alone | Markers show syntax, not intent — you need each side's diff from the merge base | `git diff $BASE..<ours> -- <path>` and the same for theirs |
| Skipping typecheck/tests before commit | Leaves broken merges as commits | Run the project's verification command; if it fails, fix before committing |
| Hand-resolving `pnpm-lock.yaml` conflict markers | Produces a lockfile no resolver would generate; `--frozen-lockfile` installs break | Resolve the `package.json` files, then regenerate the lockfile (Phase 3) |
| Only typecheck/test after a dep-touching merge | Bundler-only breakage (missing transitive export, etc.) passes both | Also run the build + `pnpm deps:lint` when the merge changed dependencies |
| Pushing after committing | User didn't ask for that | Stop at Phase 4; push is a separate ask |

## Quick Reference

**Merge command recipe (after approval):**
```bash
git merge main --no-commit --no-ff
# ... apply per-file resolutions via Edit tool ...
# pnpm-lock.yaml: do NOT Edit — resolve the package.json files, then regenerate (Phase 3)
grep -rn '^<<<<<<< \|^>>>>>>> ' <touched-paths>   # expect no output
<typecheck>   # + build & pnpm deps:lint if deps changed
git add <resolved-paths>
git commit --no-edit
```

**Rebase recipe (after approval):**
```bash
git rebase <target>
# per commit that conflicts:
#   - apply resolution via Edit
#   - git add <paths>
#   - git rebase --continue
<typecheck>   # after the whole rebase finishes
```

**Resuming an in-progress merge you didn't start:** treat the current state as mid-Phase-3. Run `git status` to find unmerged paths, then loop back to Phase 2 on those files: read each side's diff from merge base, tag, propose, wait for approval — don't resolve blind.

## Red Flags — Stop and Restart the Phase

- About to run `git merge` / `git rebase` without having run `git merge-tree` → back to Phase 1
- About to resolve conflicts without having surfaced tags + proposal → back to Phase 2
- Auto-merged file not classified → back to Phase 2
- About to commit without running project verification → back to Phase 3
- About to Edit `pnpm-lock.yaml` or another generated artifact to clear conflict markers → stop; resolve its source and regenerate (Phase 3)
- About to push → stop; that's not this skill's job

gh pr create --base main --title "refactor(web): simplify apps/web, drop unloaded Sentry stubs, fix blog JSON-LD address" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

A behavior-preserving simplification pass over `apps/web`, plus one small fix that does change output.

**Simplifications (rendered output unchanged)**
- **Rebake panel:** `Deck` derives its own button labels from `isRebaking`/`isFetching` instead of the panel choosing them and `Deck` repeating the choice. `readout()` loses a nested `if` with a duplicated return.
- **Playground shared pieces:** one `LandedRows` for the row map `stage.tsx` and `row.tsx` both carried; `tickLabelStyle()` replaces a nested ternary in the timeline axis; `og-demo` fetches the `endpoint` it already derived; `STATE_SOURCE` is a single literal; `LivePanel.className` and `CodeBlock.lang` go (no caller passed either); `parseRunId` has one guard.
- **API and lib:** `addSubscriberContact()` in `lib/subscribers.ts` replaces the identical Resend contact call in both confirm routes (same position in the same `Promise.all`); `ticketRedirect(ticket, request)` reads the protocol off the request instead of a boolean both callers computed identically; one `errorResponse()` builds the confirm route's five error bodies, same JSON.
- **Pages and components:** `ogCard()` replaces the 12-line openGraph/twitter block five pages carried; `ASIDE_LINK_CLASS` is declared once beside `MetaAside`; `MetaAside.noMarker` and `Sidebar.tags` were dead and are removed; the FAQ shape is declared once.
- Stale comments corrected (nemo, the `/ingest` rewrite, "Re-baking…", the state chapter's re-render pass and press annotation).

**Removed**
- `sentry.server.config.ts` and `sentry.edge.config.ts`. Sentry's manual setup has `instrumentation.ts` import these from `register()`; `@sentry/nextjs` 10 auto-loads only the client config. Here `register()` reaches `@repo/observability`'s `server`/`edge` modules directly, so nothing imported the two files.

**Fix (changes output)**
- Blog posts' JSON-LD `mainEntityOfPage` was built from `VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL` with `https` chosen only if the value started with "https". Vercel sets a bare hostname, so production emits `http://www.hastoggle.dev/blog/…`. It now resolves against `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_URL`, the base the root layout uses for `metadataBase`.

## Not in this PR
- `instrumentation.ts` does not export `onRequestError = Sentry.captureRequestError`, which Sentry's guide recommends for Server Component, route handler and proxy errors.
- `MarketingButton`'s `brand`/`secondary` variants and `Navbar`/`PlusGrid`'s `variant` are never used with another value; left as design options.
- `boundary/card.tsx` has "client" branches that cannot render; `copy.test.ts` pins those tables as the lesson.
- The interior-page frame is duplicated across five files; extracting it needs slots and a DOM diff on a preview.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun test` in `apps/web` — 189 pass, no test modified
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] Biome clean
- [x] `next build` succeeds (run locally with a placeholder `UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET`; the workspace env does not set it)
- [x] Built `/lab` emits the same `og:image`/`twitter:card` tags as before
- [x] Built blog post emits `https://www.hastoggle.dev/blog/<slug>` in `mainEntityOfPage`
- [x] Merged `origin/main` (#458) with no conflicts; gates re-run on the merged tree
- [ ] Preview deploy: press through the rebake panel (both views), the stream stage, the OG image demo, and submit the waitlist form once

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

I want to weigh each option honestly, starting with onRequestError: Sentry recommends it and it's a single line, but since production has no Sentry DSN configured, it would effectively be a no-op right now. It's a low-risk, server-side-only addition, so I'm weighing whether it's really worth including in a simplification-focused PR.

I'd hold off on onRequestError for now since it's a behavior change and the PR is already mixed — better to split it into its own small PR since it belongs in packages/observability, benefiting all three apps at once. For MarketingButton, the dead brand/secondary variants are safe to remove and cheap to include, though Eric asked to leave things as-is, while the navbar variant should stay since it's intentionally documented. The boundary card and page frame changes both need separate design decisions or preview diffing, so those stay out of scope too — overall I'd merge as is, with onRequestError as the one thing worth a follow-up PR.

content.text:
None of the open items need to land before you merge; two are worth doing soon and two I'd drop.

- **`MarketingButton`'s `brand` and `secondary` variants — fold into this PR.** Nothing renders them, and `tsc` would catch any caller I missed. They hard-code `bg-white` and `text-slate-950`, so they would break in dark mode if anyone did use them. The change is a 15-line deletion in one file, and I can add it now.
- **`onRequestError` — do it next, as its own PR.**
  - **What it fixes:** the missing export is a real gap against Sentry's setup guide, and it takes one line. It belongs in `packages/observability/instrumentation.ts` so that `apps/app` and `apps/api` get it too, which takes it outside a web-only refactor.
  - **Timing:** it isn't urgent. As of your 2026-09-15 env audit, prod has no Sentry DSN, so nothing is lost today. Land it before you turn the DSN on, because otherwise server-side errors will be missing from Sentry.
- **`Navbar`/`PlusGrid` `variant` — leave it.** The prop carries a comment explaining the light/dark band, so it looks like deliberate headroom for a dark section.
- **Unreachable "client" branches in `boundary/card.tsx` — leave them.** `copy.test.ts` pins both tables as the statement of the lesson. Removing the branches would mean rewording those tests, which is a design decision about the chapter. If the dead arms bother you, a one-line comment saying the orange arm is reserved is the cheap option.
- **Interior-page frame duplication — leave it for a separate PR.** It is the biggest duplication left, but three of the five sites need an escape hatch, and the only way to verify it is a DOM diff on a preview deploy. Bundling it here would make this PR harder to review.

Should I add the `MarketingButton` cleanup to #460?

name: web-prod-env-optional-services-absent

As of 2026-09-15, `vercel env ls production` for `has-toggle-dev-web` lists only: BASEHUB_TOKEN, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, LOGTAIL_*, MONGODB_URI, NEXT_PUBLIC_{APP,WEB}_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_{HOST,KEY}, NEXT_PUBLIC_BETTER_STACK_*, RECONCILE_SECRET, RESEND_* (4), VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL, HAS_TOGGLE_SOURCE_MAP_UPLOAD.

**Why:** Several protections in the code are env-gated and silently off in production: Arcjet (`ARCJET_KEY`), the Upstash rate limiter, GA, the Sentry DSN, Abstract deliverability. That is why `apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts` falls back to an in-memory window.

**How to apply:** Don't assume a scaffold-era guard is live in prod; check env names first (`bunx vercel env ls production` after `vercel link --project has-toggle-dev-web --scope spiritsdontfly`). Stronger rate limiting without code = Vercel WAF rule. Related: [[env-quirks]], [[hastoggle-positioning]].

As of 2026-09-15, `vercel env ls production` for `has-toggle-dev-web` lists only: BASEHUB_TOKEN, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, LOGTAIL_*, MONGODB_URI, NEXT_PUBLIC_{APP,WEB}_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_{HOST,KEY}, NEXT_PUBLIC_BETTER_STACK_*, RECONCILE_SECRET, RESEND_* (4), VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL, HAS_TOGGLE_SOURCE_MAP_UPLOAD.

content.text:
First confirm the two merged PRs behave in production. After that, the most valuable next piece of work is the Sentry sampling config.

**Check now**
1. **Sentry receives server errors.** Once the #462 deploy is live, look for a server-side event in Sentry. I couldn't test this locally because this workspace has no DSN.
2. **The #460 UI on the live site.** Press through the rebake panel in both views, the stream stage and the OG image demo. Submit the waitlist form once, because that path uses the shared contact helper and the new `ticketRedirect`.

**Next work, in the order I'd do it**
1. **Sentry volume.**
   - `packages/observability/server.ts` and `edge.ts` set `tracesSampleRate: 1`.
   - They also forward every `console.log`, `warn` and `error` to Sentry as logs.
   - With the DSN live, that traces 100% of requests and ships all console output, which uses quota and can cost money.
   - I'd lower the sample rate and forward only `warn` and `error`. I haven't looked at your Sentry plan or usage, so treat the urgency as a guess.
2. **Same Sentry stubs in the other apps.** `apps/app` and `apps/api` still have the `sentry.server.config.ts` and `sentry.edge.config.ts` files that #460 removed from web. `apps/app/proxy.ts` also still mentions createNEMO in a comment. It's a small cleanup PR.
3. **Blog posts have no canonical link.** I noticed this while fixing the JSON-LD address. It would be one addition to `generateMetadata`. It does change rendered output, so it's your decision.
4. **Interior-page frame duplication.** This is the largest duplication left, spread across five files. It needs a DOM diff on a preview, so it should be its own PR.

**Small items**
- The header comment in `lib/rate-limit.ts` says "the two forms that send mail", but `rebakeShell` uses the limiter too.
- The `/remember` handoff has been pending since 2026-09-17, and the session hook keeps re-delivering the old one. Running `/remember` would replace it with today's state.

Should I start on the Sentry sampling config?

content.text:
Saved.

**Item 4, the duplicated page frame.**

- **What it is:** five pages share the same outer skeleton: Contents, Articles, Contact, the 404 page and the error page. Each has the navbar, a two-column grid with an empty left rail, an eyebrow label, a big `h1`, a lede, the page's own content, and the footer. That is about 20 lines copy-pasted into each of the five files.
- **Why it matters:** nothing is broken. But if you change the heading size or the rail width, you have to make the same edit five times, and missing one makes that page drift.
- **The fix:** one `PageFrame` component, so each page shrinks to just its copy and content.
- **The catch:** three of the five pages each deviate from the shared skeleton.
  - The error page is a client component, so it can't import the cached server footer.
  - The lab heading has an extra width cap.
  - The blog page puts its JSON-LD before the navbar.
  - The frame needs an option for each, which erodes most of the gain. There are no tests for this markup, so the only check is an HTML diff of all five pages on a preview.
- **Recommendation:** skip it for now. Do it the next time you redesign the interior pages or add a sixth one.

**PR #463** (https://github.com/hasToggle/hasToggle.dev/pull/463) has the rest, in three commits.

- **Sentry volume:**
  - `tracesSampleRate` goes from 1 to 0.1 in the server, edge and browser setups.
  - Only `console.warn` and `console.error` are forwarded now. `console.log` was being sent as Sentry logs, and no app code uses it on purpose.
  - Errors are still reported unsampled.
  - Both values live in a new `packages/observability/sampling.ts`.
  - I left the Session Replay rates alone, since `apps/web` doesn't load Replay.
- **Leftover stubs and comments:**
  - `apps/app` and `apps/api` lose the same unloaded `sentry.*.config.ts` files that #460 removed from web.
  - The createNEMO comment in `apps/app/proxy.ts` is fixed.
  - The `rate-limit.ts` header comment now mentions the shell demo, which uses the limiter too.
- **Blog canonical:**
  - Posts now emit `<link rel="canonical" href="https://www.hastoggle.dev/blog/<slug>">`. I checked this in the built HTML.
  - I first wrote it as a relative URL. That inherited the same broken local base as `og:image`, so I switched to one `postUrl()` built on `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_URL`. The JSON-LD address uses the same function, so the two can't drift.

**Verification for #463**
- `tsc` passes in all three apps and the observability package.
- The 189 web tests pass, and `next build` for `apps/web` succeeds.
- Biome is clean on every touched file. One existing `useDestructuring` error remains in `client-without-replay.ts`, which this PR doesn't touch.
- I typechecked `apps/app` and `apps/api` but did not build or run them.
- I couldn't verify the Sentry changes locally because this workspace has no DSN. After deploy, check that errors still arrive and that transaction and log volume drops.
